title: Heap basics
learn: complete binary tree in an array, sift up/down, heapify O(n), `heapq` (min-heap; negate for max), heap sort
hook: Whenever a problem says "repeatedly take the largest" or "always process the most urgent next", the answer is a heap. It's also the engine behind Dijkstra, schedulers and every top-k question that follows.

explain.prompt: Explain what a binary heap is, how push and pop keep it valid, and their time complexity.
keyPoints: a complete binary tree where every parent ≤ its children (min-heap), stored in an array
children of index i are 2i + 1 and 2i + 2, parent is (i − 1) // 2
push: append at the end, sift up while smaller than the parent: O(log n)
pop: take the root, move the last element to the root, sift down with the smaller child: O(log n)
peek is O(1); heapify builds a heap in O(n); Python's heapq is a min-heap (negate for max)
